review.reason:
Four of the five predictions held. The fifth failed, and the overlays show errors that a rotation check cannot detect. (1) worst_consistency_ratio is 0.522, within the ≤1.0 target. (2) Aspect ratio is the binding term as predicted (0.522, against 0.223 for S and 0.172 for direction). (3) The direction difference is at most 1.46° on the 10 images with S ≥ 0.3. The 3 images with S < 0.3 report no direction difference, so they were excluded. (4) The median S difference is 0.0067. (5) The median estimator gap is 0.147, not ≤ 0.10, and 9 of 13 images are above 0.10, with gaps up to 0.34 on Ti64_34. Flake-based S (median 0.54) and tensor S (about 0.15–0.58) disagree systematically on real images, so it is not settled which S the pipeline should report. Confidence is high in the consistency numbers, but they show only that the errors are the same at every angle.

Overlays:
- Colony boundaries are kept well. In Ti64_28 the boundary between the pink and yellow colonies is clean, with no flake crossing it.
- The wide straight grain-boundary-alpha bands are left grey rather than counted: the band in Ti64_21 running from lower left to centre, and the long diagonal in Ti64_34. That is the right outcome.
- Laths are clearly cut into short brick-like pieces along their length: the orange/yellow colony at the top right of Ti64_21, the centre and right of Ti64_34, and the top of Ti64_28. Median aspect ratio is 2.5–3.4 on most images. Continuous alpha laths in lamellar or colony Ti-6Al-4V usually have aspect ratios of roughly 5–20, so the absolute aspect ratio is very likely underestimated. Self-consistency cannot see this.
- Grey (excluded) bands between coloured laths are often as wide as the laths themselves, especially in Ti64_28. Real beta ribs are much thinner than alpha laths. So a large share of laths is probably being merged or rejected as branched, which biases the statistics toward compact fragments.
- No scratches were found on any of the 13 images. There is no false scratch, but scratch recall on real data is untested. The straight diagonal band in Ti64_34 has similar orientation on both sides; it is most likely grain-boundary alpha, but I cannot rule out a scratch from the overlay.
- 5 of 13 mean directions lie within 3° of 0/180°. The small 30° rotation differences argue against a grid bias, but a single test angle is not enough to exclude it.
review.next_step:
1. Reduce cuts along the length. Change h_px 1.5 -> 2.5, so that shallower watershed seeds merge and fewer cross-cuts appear in laths, and boundary_sensitivity 1.0 -> 0.8, so that weak transverse contrast inside a lath is no longer read as a boundary. Run this on Ti64 dev and on synthetic dev in the same iteration, because synthetic dev is the guard against merging across colony boundaries. Accept only if synthetic worst_family stays ≤ 1.0, real worst_consistency_ratio stays ≤ 1.0, and median real aspect ratio rises toward 4 or more without merges across colony boundaries in the overlays.
2. Add two evaluator outputs, which are not method parameters: the area fraction of grey (excluded) flakes per image, and rotation checks at 15°, 45° and 90° as well as 30°. These quantify the exclusion bias and the possible pull toward 0°.
3. Leave scratch_min_contrast at 0.07 and scratch_min_length_px at 140. Zero detections on real images neither supports nor refutes scratch handling. To test it, paste synthetic scratches of known position onto Ti64 dev images and measure recall and whether flakes are cut or merged across them. Parallel-scratch recall still needs the global Hough/RANSAC line step; no current parameter fixes it.
4. The estimator gap cannot be fixed by a parameter. Decide which S estimator is the reported one, flake-based or tensor, and drop the ≤ 0.10 gap claim until then.
